title: Spleen anatomy: red pulp and white pulp
description: The largest lymphoid organ: a blood filter, immune sentinel and red-cell graveyard.

questions.question: What is the spleen's function?
questions.answer: The spleen filters blood, removes aging red blood cells and helps immune cells respond to blood-borne material. Its red and white pulp perform different tasks.

questions.question: Can you feel a normal spleen?
questions.answer: A normal adult spleen is usually protected beneath the left lower ribs and is not readily felt on examination; enlargement is a medical finding, not something this atlas can diagnose.

questions.question: What is the capsule & trabeculae?
questions.answer: A fibroelastic capsule sending trabeculae into the pulp, carrying the vessels. Function: Structural framework and conduit for vessels.

questions.question: Where is the white pulp located?
questions.answer: Periarteriolar lymphoid sheaths (T cells), follicles (B cells) and a marginal zone rich in macrophages. Function: Immune surveillance of blood: antibody and opsonin production, especially against capsules.

questions.question: What is the function of the hilum?
questions.answer: Function: Vascular gateway; also the site of accessory spleens in ~15% of people. The notched medial border where splenic vessels enter and the tail of pancreas and stomach fundus relate.
